title: Djokovic Battles Past Borges at China Open for First Win Since Wimbledon
summary:
Novak Djokovic is back in the winner's circle. The 39-year-old beat Nuno Borges at the China Open on Wednesday for his first victory since reaching the Wimbledon semi-finals in July. He won 6-3, 7-6 (7-2) in one hour and 50 minutes.

It was far from easy. Djokovic struggled in the second set against the Portuguese player. He used his racquet to stretch his back between games and needed a medical timeout to treat his right shoulder. In August, Djokovic revealed he has an underlying health condition that causes particular issues in hot, humid conditions and has affected him for "the past couple of years."

Despite the struggles, Djokovic maintained his remarkable unbeaten record at the China Open. The win was his 30th consecutive victory in Beijing, though it was his first appearance at the event since 2015 — 11 years away from the tournament. The Serb, a 24-time Grand Slam champion and former world number one, is bidding to win the China Open for a record-extending seventh time. He has won six titles there between 2009 and 2015.

Next up, Djokovic faces wildcard Bu Yunchaokete of China in the second round.

In the women's draw, Great Britain's Katie Boulter advanced with a straight-set win over Mai Hontama of Japan. Boulter, 30, claimed a 6-3, 6-4 victory and will now face Czech seventh seed Karolina Muchova in the next round.
why_it_matters: Elite sport is rarely only about talent — it is also about managing a body that ages and a schedule that wears players down, which is why Djokovic's return raises questions about how long the greats can stay competitive. It also shows how one tournament's record can define a career, and how the women's and men's draws on the same tour tell linked stories about who gets the spotlight next.

background_read: Novak Djokovic (Serbia's tennis star, who holds the men's record of 24 Grand Slam singles titles) has been at the top of men's tennis for nearly two decades. The Grand Slams (the sport's four biggest tournaments — the Australian Open, the French Open, Wimbledon and the US Open) are the events players build their seasons around, and Wimbledon is the oldest of them.

The China Open (an annual tournament in Beijing that hosts both men's and women's draws) was cancelled for several years during the COVID-19 pandemic, which helps explain why Djokovic had not played there since 2015. In tennis, a 'wildcard' is a free entry given to a player who did not qualify on ranking, while a 'seed' is a top-ranked player placed in the draw so the strongest players do not meet too early.

Tennis is played on different surfaces — grass at Wimbledon, clay in Paris and hard courts in Beijing — and hard courts in hot, humid weather are among the most physically demanding conditions, which matters for any player managing a health condition.

perspectives.description: Djokovic's fans point to a 30-match winning streak in Beijing and 24 Grand Slam titles as evidence of extraordinary consistency. Winning in straight sets after a long absence, while visibly uncomfortable, is exactly the kind of resilience that has kept him at the top.

Physically, the picture looks worrying: a medical timeout for his shoulder and a declared condition that flares up in heat and humidity. Critics argue that at 39 he should play a lighter schedule, and that pushing through pain in difficult conditions risks turning a manageable problem into a serious injury.

perspectives.perspective: Neutral — the pattern of one-tournament dominance
perspectives.description: The China Open numbers reveal something statisticians often note: some players simply match up well with a particular court, crowd and ball, and their record there becomes far better than their overall record. His long absence also reflects a wider real-world factor — tournament calendars were disrupted for years during the pandemic, so gaps in records are not always about form.

perspectives.perspective: Forward-looking — what the result could lead to
perspectives.description: The immediate test comes in the next round against home wildcard Bu Yunchaokete, and a deep run would put a seventh Beijing title within reach. Beyond that week, the result is a small signal at the start of a season, and the bigger question is how the tour handles great players whose bodies need careful management.
